problem_statement: ColorlibHQ/AdminLTE is a runnable AdminLTE v4 static Bootstrap 5 admin-dashboard template served from its prebuilt static output (dist/): an operations shell with a fixed sidebar navigation, a top navbar, a KPI small-box row, dashboard cards, a Direct Chat widget and a shared footer, plus reference inner pages including a Chat page (pages/chat.html) and a User Profile page (pages/profile.html). Out of the box every page is the generic AdminLTE demo: the sidebar wordmark reads 'AdminLTE 4', the page titles read 'AdminLTE v4 | Dashboard' / 'AdminLTE 4 | Chat' / 'AdminLTE 4 | User Profile', the dashboard header reads 'Dashboard', the four KPI small-boxes are labelled 'New Orders', 'Bounce Rate', 'User Registrations' and 'Unique Visitors', the dashboard card reads 'Direct Chat', the Chat page header reads 'Chat' with a generic design-review conversation, the Profile page header reads 'User Profile' with a generic 'Product Designer' persona, and the footer credits 'AdminLTE.io'. Rework the demo into a single coherent fictional admin product, 'Northwind Ops', a field-operations and crew-dispatch console. Rebrand consistently ACROSS the whole shell and the inner Chat and Profile pages while preserving the AdminLTE design language (sidebar, navbar, small-box KPI cards, Bootstrap 5 utilities, cards and footer): the sidebar wordmark and all page titles become Northwind Ops, the dashboard header becomes 'Operations Dashboard', the four KPI small-boxes carry operations labels (New Dispatch Jobs, Missed SLA Rate, New Crew Onboarded, Active Field Sites), the dashboard chat card becomes the 'Dispatch Desk', the Chat page becomes a crew-dispatch 'Dispatch Desk' conversation about routing crews between field sites, and the Profile page becomes a 'Crew Profile' for a 'Lead Dispatch Coordinator'. Keep the sidebar/navbar navigation, cards and footer intact and reachable, keep every page free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile, and do not leave the inner Chat and Profile pages (or the KPI row) as the original AdminLTE demo while only relabelling the hero wordmark. In addition to the rebrand, add a shared operational status rail — the 'Dispatch shift board' — to the top of the content area of the dashboard, the Dispatch Desk (Chat) and the Crew Profile pages. The shift board is a compact card that surfaces the current shift's live metrics as a row of four tiles (Open jobs, Crews on shift, Avg response, Board status) and a shift readout line that names whether the console is running on the Day board or the Night board. Because it reports shift-wide status it must appear on every operational screen (dashboard, Dispatch Desk and Crew Profile) as one shared component, styled in the console's light 'operations card' palette (light surface, subtle border, primary-accent title, tinted tiles) to match the AdminLTE small-box idiom. The metric-tile row must wrap fluidly so the shift board never causes horizontal overflow on desktop or at 390px mobile. The shift readout must stay wired to the AdminLTE light/dark theme control: clicking the theme dropdown's Dark option must switch the console to the Night board AND update the readout line to read 'Night board' (and back to 'Day board' for Light) — the readout must re-read the live theme after every toggle, not display a value captured once at load. Do not bolt the shift board onto only the dashboard, do not collapse it into an off-palette dark slab, do not lay its tiles on a fixed non-wrapping track that overflows narrow phones, and do not leave the shift readout showing a stale 'Day board' after the console has switched to the Night board.
required_content: The sidebar wordmark and the page titles across the dashboard, Chat and Profile pages read as the Northwind Ops field-operations console instead of the generic 'AdminLTE 4' / 'AdminLTE v4 | Dashboard' demo branding.

The dashboard header reads 'Operations Dashboard' and the four KPI small-boxes carry operations labels (New Dispatch Jobs, Missed SLA Rate, New Crew Onboarded, Active Field Sites) instead of the demo 'New Orders' / 'Bounce Rate' / 'User Registrations' / 'Unique Visitors' labels, while preserving the small-box KPI pattern.

The Chat page is rebranded into a crew-dispatch 'Dispatch Desk' conversation (routing crews between field sites, SLA and site-status coordination) instead of the demo design-review chat, with the page header reading 'Dispatch Desk'.
The Profile page is rebranded into a 'Crew Profile' for a 'Lead Dispatch Coordinator' at the Northwind Regional Depot instead of the demo 'User Profile' / 'Product Designer' persona.

The AdminLTE sidebar/navbar navigation, dashboard cards, avatars and shared footer remain intact, reachable and free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile; the footer credit no longer reads AdminLTE.io.

A shared 'Dispatch shift board' status rail (title 'Dispatch shift board', a row of four metric tiles — Open jobs, Crews on shift, Avg response, Board status — and a shift readout line) appears at the top of the content area on the dashboard, the Dispatch Desk (Chat) page AND the Crew Profile page as one consistent shared component in the light operations-card palette.

The shift board's metric-tile row wraps fluidly so neither the dashboard nor the Chat page has any horizontal overflow at 390px mobile; the shift board is not laid out on a fixed non-wrapping track that overflows the phone.

The shift readout line stays wired to the AdminLTE theme control: after clicking the Dark theme option the console switches to the Night board and the readout line reads 'Night board' (re-read from the live theme), not a stale 'Day board' captured at load.
design_constraints: Preserve the AdminLTE v4 design language: the fixed sidebar navigation, top navbar, the KPI small-box row, the dashboard cards, Bootstrap 5 utility classes, the bg-* small-box palette and the shared footer.

Rebrand consistently across the whole shell and the inner Chat and Profile pages rather than relabelling only the sidebar wordmark and page titles while leaving inner pages and the KPI row as the demo.
Use a single coherent Northwind Ops field-operations identity (dispatch jobs, crews, field sites, SLAs, the Dispatch Desk and crew coordination) across the dashboard, Chat and Profile pages.
Use the in-repo local imagery and icon fonts (assets/img avatars/logo, the vendored Bootstrap Icons) rather than remote stock imagery or icon packs; do not introduce external network dependencies.
Keep the dashboard, Chat and Profile pages free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile and keep the sidebar/navbar/footer chrome intact.

The Dispatch shift board is a single shared component rendered identically on the dashboard, Chat and Profile pages (not a per-page one-off); its metric row wraps fluidly and it uses the light operations-card palette that matches the AdminLTE small-box surfaces, never an off-palette dark slab.
The shift readout must reflect the live AdminLTE theme (Day board for light, Night board for dark) and re-sync on every theme toggle rather than caching the label once at wire time.

Give the shared shift board BEM-style class hooks so it is identifiable across all three pages: the title element (text 'Dispatch shift board') carries class shift-board__title, and the live shift readout line (text 'Day board' / 'Night board') carries class shift-board__readout.
state_constraints: desktop_home captures the operations dashboard: the Northwind Ops sidebar wordmark, the 'Operations Dashboard' header, the four rebranded KPI small-boxes (New Dispatch Jobs / Missed SLA Rate / New Crew Onboarded / Active Field Sites) and the 'Dispatch Desk' dashboard card, with the AdminLTE navbar/sidebar/footer chrome intact and no horizontal overflow.
mobile_home and tablet_home capture the same dashboard at 390px and tablet width, where the sidebar collapses but the KPI row and cards stay readable with no horizontal overflow.

desktop_chat and mobile_chat capture the Chat page rebranded into the crew-dispatch 'Dispatch Desk' conversation (the page header reads 'Dispatch Desk' and the messages route crews between field sites) at desktop and 390px mobile.

desktop_profile captures the Profile page rebranded into a 'Crew Profile' for a 'Lead Dispatch Coordinator' at the Northwind Regional Depot, preserving the AdminLTE profile card, activity and about panels.

Source inspection confirms the site is the prebuilt AdminLTE v4 static dist output served without a build step, with the generic AdminLTE demo branding on the shell and the Chat/Profile inner pages and local avatar/logo imagery under assets/img.

desktop_home, desktop_chat and desktop_profile each show the shared Dispatch shift board rail at the top of the content area (title 'Dispatch shift board' with four metric tiles and a shift readout) in the light operations-card palette, proving the component is consistent across all three operational screens.
mobile_home and mobile_chat capture the dashboard and Chat page at 390px where the shift board's metric tiles wrap onto multiple rows with no horizontal overflow.

change_completion: The dashboard, Chat and Profile pages all carry one coherent Northwind Ops field-operations identity.
The generic AdminLTE demo branding, the demo KPI labels, the demo design-review chat and the demo 'Product Designer' profile no longer dominate the captured pages.
The AdminLTE sidebar/navbar navigation, cards, avatars and footer remain functional and reachable.
The shared Dispatch shift board appears on the dashboard, Chat and Profile pages with its four metric tiles and shift readout.
design_consistency: The rebrand preserves the AdminLTE v4 design language: sidebar, navbar, small-box KPI palette, cards and footer rhythm.
The Northwind Ops identity is applied consistently across the shell and the inner Chat and Profile pages rather than only on the hero wordmark.

The dashboard, Chat and Profile pages remain reachable through the AdminLTE sidebar/navbar navigation.
The shift readout stays synced to the live AdminLTE theme, reading Night board after the Dark toggle and Day board for Light.

The sidebar collapses and the KPI row, cards and chat panel wrap cleanly on mobile.
The shift board's metric-tile row wraps with no horizontal overflow at 390px on both the dashboard and the Chat page.

author_notes: Repo-grounded AdminLTE v4 static-dashboard modify/Edit (implementation_continuity) task. Runability passes through the prebuilt static dist output served with a plain static file server. Captures show a polished AdminLTE shell but generic demo branding on the dashboard, KPI row, Chat and Profile pages. The task asks for a coherent Northwind Ops field-operations rebrand across the dashboard, Chat and Profile pages, testing cross-page brand/content consistency and preservation of the AdminLTE design system without issue/PR framing. DECLARED INFRASTRUCTURE (identical across reference, baseline and bad, NOT task content): the AdminLTE dist loads its Bootstrap 5 / Popper / Bootstrap-Icons / OverlayScrollbars / ApexCharts / jsVectorMap / SortableJS runtime and the Source Sans 3 web font from the jsDelivr CDN; those remote <link>/<script> references are vendored to a local ./vendor directory (with the Bootstrap Icons woff2/woff fonts) and the remote Source Sans 3 font <link> is dropped in favour of the AdminLTE font fallback stack, so all three legs serve entirely offline with zero external network requests. This vendoring is applied identically to every leg. The baseline is the original AdminLTE demo (generic branding on every page). The bad solution rebrands only the sidebar wordmark and the page titles (the hero) but leaves the KPI row, the Chat page and the Profile page as the AdminLTE demo, so it preserves the navigation (passing regression) but fails the cross-page completion, visible-text, forbidden-text and DOM-assertion gates. L4 HARDEN (2026-07-05): the rebrand is extended with a shared 'Dispatch shift board' rail carried on the dashboard, Chat and Profile pages, which layers four orthogonal discriminators onto the task. DECLARED INFRASTRUCTURE (identical across all three legs, NOT task content): a scoped sc-infra.css neutralises AdminLTE's app-wrapper / app-main max-width:100vw and wrapper overflow-x clamps so the shift board's real horizontal overflow becomes observable at the document level (measurement-enabling, not a fix); the shared shift-board markup and the readout-sync script are injected identically. The graded, leg-varying source is css/shift-board.css (layout + palette of the shift board) and js/shift-board.js (the readout theme-sync wiring). The reference wraps the metric row fluidly (no overflow), renders the board on all three pages, uses the light operations-card palette and re-reads the live theme. The baseline is the original unrepaired layout defect: the board sits on a fixed 760px non-wrapping track that overflows 390px mobile (fails no_horizontal_overflow) and the board is present only on the dashboard (fails the cross-page shift-board dom_assertions on the Chat and Profile pages), while its palette and theme wiring are correct (so it passes interaction_assertions). The bad solution is a competent-looking but wrong shortcut: it narrows the track to 560px and adds overflow-x:hidden to the row (the document still overflows on mobile, so no_horizontal_overflow still fails), restyles the board into an off-palette dark-teal slab (fails visual_regression against the light reference), omits the board from the Profile page (fails the cross-page dom_assertion there) and wires the readout with a stale closure so it keeps reading 'Day board' after the Night-board toggle (fails interaction_assertions even though the click is a real, succeeded interaction). Design keywords: shift board, operations card, dispatch, crew, layout, palette, responsive wrap, theme readout.
